contract.lambda_timing: r30_train.train_arm_seed freezes lam = state['lambda'] for the whole batch, runs the four rollouts, calls ppo_update, and only then dual_update; so every batch's actor is trained with the PRE-update lambda and lambda_next takes effect from the next batch's rollout. Verified field-by-field, not assumed.
contract.objective: c = C/B0; g = E[Y_ref] - E[Y_policy] - delta; L_max = -E[c] - lambda*g; A_actor = lambda*A_task - A_cost
contract.reference_is_a_scalar: batch_g_hat reads the cached immediate on-time count as a plain float, so it carries no gradient into the actor
contract.source_of_truth: v2_trainer (correctness-v2) + cost_math (Stage A), as frozen and referenced by ROUND30; nothing here redefines the training math

inputs.non_finite_checks: every lambda/g_hat/update field of all 192 batch records

reading_notes: the training trajectory is the SAMPLED policy's constraint trajectory; the greedy decode has its own numbers only in ABSOLUTE_PERFORMANCE.json and may not be read off these g_hat values
g_hat here is a 4-episode paired point estimate per batch; a batch mean of 0 can still contain individual scenes with loss and others with gain
a curve that is still moving at batch 31 only shows the run had not stabilised; it does not establish that more training would help
section: constraint and dual-variable trajectories rebuilt from ROUND30 batch records, training rows, reference rows and tapes (0 launches, 0 optimizer .step)
